dialog.deleteNodesAndFolders: Delete nodes and remove empty folders?
dialog.deleteNodePermanent: This permanently deletes the node — this cannot be undone.
dialog.deleteNodesPermanent: This permanently deletes all {count} nodes — this cannot be undone.
dialog.onlyNamedFolders: Only the named empty folders are removed.
dialog.keptNote: Sessions, imported source records, and non-empty folders are kept.
dialog.deleteSessionBody: This permanently removes the session — its messages, background jobs, and extraction records. Everything it added to the graph stays unless you check below. This cannot be undone.
dialog.tracesBody: This session's topics, links, and events leave the graph too. Topics other sessions or imported notes also cover survive; topics only this session created are removed entirely.
dialog.abortTurnLine: The partial answer stays in the transcript.
dialog.dismissQuestionLine: Skipped — the teacher moves on without it.
dialog.discardProblemLine: The problem is dropped — no solution is revealed.
dialog.contributionsLine: Removes these sources' contributions to propositions and reasoning chains. Knowledge supported by other sources survives; knowledge supported only by these sources is removed.
dialog.diskLine: Imported source records are removed, but original files on disk are never changed. Selected folders are removed only when empty; folders needed by kept sessions remain.
dialog.alsoDeleteSessions: Also delete the {count} selected {count, plural, one {session} other {sessions}}
dialog.sessionsNote: Unchecked, conversations stay in their current folders and can be extracted again. Either way, their graph contributions and extraction coverage are cleared. Checking this also permanently deletes their messages and background jobs.
dialog.extractionRunning: An extraction is running — try again when the activity dock drains.

settingsPlugins.trustWarning: Only enable plugins you trust. Plugins run trusted local code with broad file and network access; they are not sandboxed. A broken plugin may require restarting LearnHarness.
settingsPlugins.installStep1: Clone or copy the plugin into the directory below, using its plugin ID as the folder name.
settingsPlugins.installStep2Before: For source projects, follow the repository’s dependency setup and run
settingsPlugins.installStep3: Refresh the list, then enable the plugin. New plugins are disabled by default.
settingsPlugins.installStep4: Restart LearnHarness after changing loaded code. Preserve data/ beside dist/ when updating.
settingsPlugins.authoringHint: Download the authoring skill for your coding agent.

flashcards.name: Flashcards
flashcards.description: Generate fact-recall cues from your knowledge graph and review them with FSRS-6. Generation uses your configured model and may incur cost. Native only; no Anki integration.

coding-questions.name: Coding questions
coding-questions.description: Teaching questions and coding practice with syntax highlighting and automatic tests using your installed tools. Runs local code with your user permissions; not sandboxed.

drawing-pad.name: Drawing Pad
drawing-pad.description: Draw over read-only question references and send your working with learner submissions.

rich-code-blocks.name: Rich code blocks
rich-code-blocks.description: Static chemical structures, musical notation and technical diagrams from SMILES, ABC and TikZ code blocks.

ui-showcase.name: UI Showcase
ui-showcase.description: An ephemeral gallery of public host UI controls, local callbacks, and native session surfaces.

resources.name: Resources
resources.description: A right-hand file browser: browse the local filesystem, preview PDFs, images, text, code and Office documents (docx/xlsx/pptx), and hand any file to the agent.
